resources.string: One example of cartilage: a magnified section of hyaline articular cartilage and the bone beneath it. The thickness of the layers and the size of the cells are schematic.
This smooth surface faces the joint cavity. The cells just beneath it are flatter than those deeper in the cartilage.
These cells sit in small spaces called lacunae and maintain the matrix around them. Deeper cells tend to line up in short columns.
Most of the tissue is matrix, not cells. The matrix contains abundant water, proteoglycans, and a fine network of type II collagen.
Below the thin, wavy boundary called the tidemark, the cartilage matrix is mineralized. This layer lies between uncalcified cartilage and bone.
A dense plate of bone supports the cartilage from below, with a lattice of trabecular bone deeper down.
